annotations.text:
DAYLIGHT — A's bones, Frappe's surface

Kept from A: the dense aligned table, monospaced figures, HSN and GST per line, function keys, everything visible without scrolling.

Taken from the Frappe screenshot: light sidebar instead of dark, white cards on a near-white ground, 9px radii, hairline borders instead of hard rules, one restrained blue doing all the work, thin line icons.

The result reads as a tool rather than a dashboard, without looking like 1990s accounting software.

THEMES ARE CHEAP — LAYOUTS ARE NOT

Every colour here is already a CSS token, so a theme is just a swapped token set: Daylight, Khata, Night counter. Adding one costs an afternoon.

What is NOT cheap is a second LAYOUT. Direction B's tile grid is a different screen, not a different skin — it would double the work on every feature after it. Worth building only if a real customer needs a touchscreen till.

The loyalty panel maps one-to-one onto settings that already exist and are tested. Discounts are marked because nothing behind them is built yet.
